builds.name: Reference: Attack-carry facilitator
builds.goal: Reference for Nami: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A hybrid healer and control enchanter who uses bounce positioning and attack or spell buffs to help allies trade and catch. Record E empowerment delivery and W bounce order. Offensive AP must compare ally damage/healing lost, with eligible item procs measured rather than granted on every bounce. Eligible healing/shielding may deliver ally buffs and repeated supportive value.
builds.summary: Eligible healing/shielding may deliver ally buffs and repeated supportive value.
testPlan: Kit question for Nami: Record E empowerment delivery and W bounce order. Offensive AP must compare ally damage/healing lost, with eligible item procs measured rather than granted on every bounce.

Start with the early core (Support quest, Helia if it can be triggered, then an ally-appropriate buff item) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use real support income and keep the quest/vision slot.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Eligible healing/shielding may deliver ally buffs and repeated supportive value. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Sends a bubble to a target area, dealing damage and stunning all enemies on impact. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Verify Helia charge/heal interaction and choose buffs for the actual ally rather than assume universal value.

The route fails Nami's stated kit question: Record E empowerment delivery and W bounce order. Offensive AP must compare ally damage/healing lost, with eligible item procs measured rather than granted on every bounce.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility. Also record allies lost while spending on personal damage.
tradeoffs: Verify Helia charge/heal interaction and choose buffs for the actual ally rather than assume universal value.
Full cost 10,250 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
The reference is a research control, not a claim of the current highest-win-rate build.
buyOrder: Support quest, Helia if it can be triggered, then an ally-appropriate buff item. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Begin with the actual support quest item; Celestial Opposition is earned by transformation, not directly bought as a 400-gold legendary. Keep buying vision.
Ardent Censer, Staff of Flowing Water, Redemption are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

kitEvidence.formula:
Nami unleashes a stream of water that bounces between allied and enemy champions. Each champion can only be hit once, and it hits up to [3] targets.Restores [55 / 80 / 105 / 130 / 155 + (0.4) × AP] Health to allies and will bounce to a nearby enemy champion. Deals [60 / 95 / 130 / 165 / 200 + (0.5) × AP] magic damage to enemies and will bounce to a nearby allied champion.
The damage and healing value is modified by [(-20 + (0.15) × AP) × (0.01)] each bounce.
Nami hurls a bubble, Stunning for [1.5] seconds and dealing [90 / 145 / 200 / 255 / 310 + (0.5) × AP] magic damage.

Nami empowers an allied champion's next [3] Attacks and Abilities for [6] seconds, causing them to Slow their targets by [(15 / 20 / 25 / 30 / 35 + (0.05) × AP) × (0.01)] for [1]s and deal an additional [20 / 35 / 50 / 65 / 80 + (0.2) × AP] magic damage.

Nami summons a tidal wave, Knocking Up for 0.5 seconds, Slowing by [70]%, and dealing [150 / 250 / 350 + (0.6) × AP] magic damage. The duration of the Slow increases based on distance the wave traveled, up to [4] seconds.

Allies hit by the wave gain double the effect of Surging Tides.
When Nami's Abilities hit allied champions, they gain [100 + (0.25) × AP] Move Speed, decaying over [1.5] seconds.

builds.name: Bounce growth
builds.summary: Test AP changing which W bounce carries most value.
builds.goal: Test AP changing which W bounce carries most value.
builds.hypothesis: W modifies each bounce by -20 plus 0.15 AP percent, so sufficient AP reverses attenuation. Deathcap and Staff raise both heal and damage ratios; Helia asks for an enemy hit before an allied heal. Cosmic speed supports safe bounce geometry.
testPlan: Required state: Three distinct champions within bounce reach, with an injured ally and recorded AP.
Log every bounce heal/damage below and above the AP attenuation crossover, with Staff inactive and active.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Broken bounce chains or farmed AP costs can lose more allied protection than they gain.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: W cannot bounce repeatedly through the same champion.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Echoes of Helia, Staff of Flowing Water, Rabadon's Deathcap, Cosmic Drive, Cryptbloom, Ionian Boots of Lucidity. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Self-blessing volley
builds.summary: Spend E's finite charges through Nami's own attacks.
builds.goal: Spend E's finite charges through Nami's own attacks.
builds.hypothesis: E grants three damaging attacks or abilities over six seconds. Self-casting permits direct observation of charge damage, while Nashor and Dusk add attack effects; W healing an ally can enable Censer's attack buff. AP also improves the passive movement burst.
testPlan: Required state: Self E, allied W heal and three safe attacks inside six seconds.
Count E charges and separate E, Nashor and Dusk packets in three attacks with and without allied healing.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Short range or consuming charges on incidental spells prevents the intended volley.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Dusk repeating on-hits is not evidence that it duplicates E charge consumption or damage.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.

Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
